 Africa Cup of Nations Qualification
 LIVE: Malawi vs Egypt | 2027 AFCON Qualifiers
 Malawi hosts Egypt on Tuesday, November 17, in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations Qualifiers. After the Pharaohs secured a commanding 5-0 victory in Cairo, the Flames will look to bounce back, while Egypt aims to move closer to securing its place at the continental tournament.
 Watch Malawi vs Egypt LIVE on beIN SPORTS 
 Malawi vs Egypt: How and Where to Watch LIVE 
 Matchday 4 of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations Qualifiers brings an important Group B encounter to Bingu National Stadium in Lilongwe , where Malawi welcomes Egypt on Tuesday, November 17.
 The Pharaohs lead Group B with seven points from three matches, ahead of Angola on goal difference, while Malawi occupies third place with three points.
 Kickoff is scheduled for 8:00 AM ET / 5:00 AM PT , with coverage beginning at 7:50 AM ET / 4:50 AM PT on beIN SPORTS CONNECT in the United States.
 Malawi Looks to Recover After Heavy Defeat in Cairo 
 Malawi , managed by Kalisto Pasuwa , enters the encounter looking to recover from a difficult run in the qualifying campaign.
 The Flames began with a 2-1 victory over South Sudan before suffering a 3-1 defeat against Angola .
 Their latest match ended in a disappointing 5-0 loss to Egypt on November 13 at Cairo International Stadium.
 Malawi conceded twice in the opening ten minutes and was already trailing 3-0 at halftime, struggling to contain Egypt's attacking players throughout the encounter.
 Following the defeat, Pasuwa acknowledged his team's slow start and defensive mistakes, particularly when losing possession.
 The coach will look to experienced players such as captain Richard Mbulu , Patrick Mwaungulu , Lanjesi Nkhoma and Mwisho Mhango to produce a stronger performance in front of the home supporters.
 Egypt Looks to Build on Historic Victory as Salah Breaks Scoring Record 
 Egypt , coached by Ali Maher , arrives in Malawi after an impressive 5-0 victory that strengthened its position at the top of Group B.
 The Pharaohs opened the scoring through Nasser Maher in the sixth minute before Omar Marmoush doubled the advantage just four minutes later.
 Mohamed Hany added a third goal before halftime, while Mohamed Salah completed the victory with two late goals, including a penalty in stoppage time.
 His brace also sparked debate over Egypt's all-time scoring record. Although initial reports credited Salah with surpassing Hossam Hassan , revised official figures put him on 68 international goals, one behind Hassan's record of 69.
 The match also marked a successful debut for Ali Maher , who replaced Hassan as head coach on November 7.
 With ten goals scored and none conceded in three qualifying matches, Egypt will look to maintain its unbeaten record and take another major step toward qualification.
 Egypt Could Move Closer to Securing Early Qualification 
 Egypt and Angola lead Group B with seven points each, while Malawi follows with three and South Sudan remains without a point.
 Angola joined Egypt on seven points after defeating South Sudan 2-0 on November 14, with both goals arriving in stoppage time.
 The top two teams will qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations , hosted by Kenya , Tanzania and Uganda .
 A victory in Lilongwe would put Egypt in a commanding position and could secure an early qualification spot, while Malawi needs a positive result to keep its hopes alive.
